**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Offline Autonomous Node Coordination

Minimal backend baseline for autonomous nodes that must keep working during long network outages and later reconcile state with explainable rules.

Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.

```bash
python -m offline_coordination status
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The current baseline exposes only a local status command. Persistent state is available via `offline_coordination.storage` and an append-only hash-chained audit log via `offline_coordination.audit`. Replication, conflict policies, security boundaries, observability, and network services are intentionally left for subsequent tasks.

content.content:
1	"""Read-only audit replication batches.
2	
3	A batch is a single UTF-8 compact JSON object (non-ASCII preserved, no
4	whitespace) terminated by exactly one ``\\n``::
5	
6	    {"after":...,"complete":...,"next":...,"records":[...],"version":1}
7	
8	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``after``, ``complete``,
9	``next``, ``records``, ``version`` and ``version`` is always the integer
10	1.  ``after`` echoes the request's ``after`` argument.  ``records`` holds
11	up to ``limit`` (at most 1000) audit records whose ``seq`` is greater
12	than ``after``, in audit order, each preserving the audit record key
13	order ``detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source`` and its original values.
14	``next`` is the seq of the last record in the batch, or ``after`` itself
15	when the batch is empty; ``complete`` is true when no record follows the
16	batch, and an empty ``records`` list is only valid when ``complete`` is
17	true.  Batches are generated solely through :func:`audit.read`, so the
18	audit log is never modified and :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
19	CorruptAuditError` and :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
20	
21	:func:`import_batch` validates a batch against this byte contract and
22	appends its records to the local log.  It returns a dict with the fixed
23	key order ``need``, ``next``, ``status``.  When the batch starts beyond
24	the local log (``after`` greater than the local last seq ``L``) nothing is
25	written and ``status`` is ``"missing"`` with ``need`` holding the gap
26	``[L + 1, after]`` and ``next`` set to ``L``.  Otherwise records already
27	present locally must match field by field (a mismatch raises
28	:class:`ValueError`); the matching prefix is skipped idempotently and
29	only the contiguous suffix past ``L`` is appended, linked to the local
30	last hash.  ``need`` is then ``None``, ``next`` is ``max(L, batch.next)``
31	and ``status`` is ``"applied"`` when records were appended, else
32	``"duplicate"``.  Any failure leaves the log untouched.
33	
34	Batches are checked only against the byte contract: canonical encoding, key
35	order, the seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
36	enforced by :func:`audit.append` on event input (the kind enum, non-empty
37	string fields) are *not* re-enforced here, so every log :func:`audit.read`
38	accepts round-trips through :func:`export_batch`/:func:`import_batch`.  The
39	append itself is atomic: when the write, flush or fsync step raises
40	:class:`OSError` the error propagates unchanged and the log is left
41	byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was missing).
42	
43	:func:`apply_remote` persists remote state applications in a version-1
44	*ledger*: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys sorted lexicographically,
45	exactly one trailing ``\\n``) with the top-level keys ``audit``,
46	``requests``, ``state`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
47	``state`` holds the current :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state,
48	``requests`` binds each accepted request id to the digest of its request,
49	and ``audit`` lists one entry per successful application in order; each
50	entry carries ``after``/``before`` state digests, the request ``id`` and
51	``source`` and a contiguous ``seq`` starting at 1, every entry after the
52	first chaining its ``before`` to the previous entry's ``after`` and the
53	last ``after`` hashing the stored state.  A missing ledger stands for the
54	request's ``base`` state with empty indexes; any existing file that fails
55	the byte, structure, state or index rules is rejected with
56	:class:`ValueError` and left untouched.
57	
58	Replaying a request whose ``id`` is already bound to exactly the same
59	request digest always yields ``duplicate`` from the saved binding alone,
60	immediately or after other commits: one item per remote record in
61	ascending key order, each already duplicate with an empty ``need`` map,
62	and no receipt; the ledger is never read for modification on a replay.
63	A bound ``id`` presented with a different request raises
64	:class:`ValueError`.  Every successful commit is one durable transaction:
65	write, flush, file sync, replacement and directory sync all lie inside
66	its boundary, and an :class:`OSError` at any stage propagates unchanged
67	with the file system restored to its pre-call state.
68	"""
69	
70	from __future__ import annotations
71	
72	import hashlib
73	import json
74	import os
75	import re
76	
77	from offline_coordination import audit, merge, storage
78	
79	AFTER = "after"
80	COMPLETE = "complete"
81	NEED = "need"
82	NEXT = "next"
83	RECORDS = "records"
84	STATUS = "status"
85	VERSION = "version"
86	
87	STATUS_MISSING = "missing"
88	STATUS_APPLIED = "applied"
89	STATUS_DUPLICATE = "duplicate"
90	
91	_BATCH_KEYS = (AFTER, COMPLETE, NEXT, RECORDS, VERSION)
92	_RESULT_KEYS = (NEED, NEXT, STATUS)
93	_RECORD_KEYS = (
94	    audit.DETAIL,
95	    audit.HASH,
96	    audit.KIND,
97	    audit.PREV,
98	    audit.SEQ,
99	    audit.SOURCE,
100	)
101	_BATCH_VERSION = 1
102	_MIN_LIMIT = 1
103	_MAX_LIMIT = 1000
104	_HEX64 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")
105	
106	
107	def export_batch(path: str, after: int = 0, limit: int = 100) -> bytes:
108	    """Return one replication batch of audit records as UTF-8 JSON bytes.
109	
110	    Selects the first ``limit`` records whose ``seq`` is greater than
111	    ``after``.  ``after`` must not exceed the log's last seq (an empty or
112	    missing log has last seq 0); otherwise :class:`ValueError` is raised.
113	
114	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError` (``bool`` is not accepted as
115	    an int); ``after < 0`` or a ``limit`` outside ``[1, 1000]`` raises
116	    :class:`ValueError`.  A corrupt log raises
117	    :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.CorruptAuditError` and filesystem
118	    errors propagate as :class:`OSError`.  The log is never modified.
119	    """
120	    if not isinstance(path, str):
121	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
122	    if isinstance(after, bool) or not isinstance(after, int):
123	        raise TypeError("after must be an int")
124	    if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int):
125	        raise TypeError("limit must be an int")
126	    if after < 0:
127	        raise ValueError("after must be >= 0")
128	    if limit < _MIN_LIMIT or limit > _MAX_LIMIT:
129	        raise ValueError("limit must be in [1, 1000]")
130	
131	    all_records = audit.read(path)
132	    last_seq = all_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if all_records else 0
133	    if after > last_seq:
134	        raise ValueError("after must not exceed the last audit seq")
135	
136	    selected = [record for record in all_records if record[audit.SEQ] > after]
137	    selected = selected[:limit]
138	    batch_records = [
139	        {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS} for record in selected
140	    ]
141	
142	    next_seq = batch_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if batch_records else after
143	    batch = {
144	        AFTER: after,
145	        COMPLETE: next_seq == last_seq,
146	        NEXT: next_seq,
147	        RECORDS: batch_records,
148	        VERSION: _BATCH_VERSION,
149	    }
150	    ordered = {key: batch[key] for key in _BATCH_KEYS}
151	    text = json.dumps(ordered, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
152	    return text.encode("utf-8")
153	
154	
155	def _invalid_batch(message: str) -> ValueError:
156	    return ValueError(f"invalid replication batch: {message}")
157	
158	
159	def _compact(obj: object) -> bytes:
160	    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
161	
162	
163	def _parse_batch(batch: bytes) -> dict:
164	    """Validate a batch against the export byte contract and decode it."""
165	    if not batch.endswith(b"\n") or batch.endswith(b"\n\n"):
166	        raise _invalid_batch("must be a single JSON object terminated by one LF")
167	    try:
168	        data = json.loads(batch[:-1].decode("utf-8"))
169	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
170	        raise _invalid_batch("is not valid UTF-8 JSON") from exc
171	
172	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or tuple(data.keys()) != _BATCH_KEYS:
173	        raise _invalid_batch(
174	            "top-level object must have exactly the keys "
175	            "'after', 'complete', 'next', 'records', 'version' in order"
176	        )
177	    version = data[VERSION]
178	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != _BATCH_VERSION:
179	        raise _invalid_batch("version must be the integer 1")
180	    for key in (AFTER, NEXT):
181	        if isinstance(data[key], bool) or not isinstance(data[key], int):
182	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be an int")
183	        if data[key] < 0:
184	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be >= 0")
185	    if not isinstance(data[COMPLETE], bool):
186	        raise _invalid_batch("complete must be a bool")
187	    records = data[RECORDS]
188	    if not isinstance(records, list):
189	        raise _invalid_batch("records must be a list")
190	    if len(records) > _MAX_LIMIT:
191	        raise _invalid_batch("records must contain at most 1000 items")
192	    if not records and not data[COMPLETE]:
193	        raise _invalid_batch("empty records require complete to be true")
194	
195	    expected_seq = data[AFTER]
196	    expected_prev = audit._ZERO_HASH if data[AFTER] == 0 else None
197	    for index, record in enumerate(records):
198	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or tuple(record.keys()) != _RECORD_KEYS:
199	            raise _invalid_batch(
200	                f"record {index} must have exactly the keys "
201	                "'detail', 'hash', 'kind', 'prev', 'seq', 'source' in order"
202	            )
203	        # Only the byte contract is enforced here: key order, the
204	        # seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
205	        # (non-empty fields, the kind enum) belong to audit.append's event
206	        # input, so records from any log audit.read accepts stay importable.
207	        prev = record[audit.PREV]
208	        digest = record[audit.HASH]
209	        if expected_prev is not None:
210	            if prev != expected_prev:
211	                raise _invalid_batch(
212	                    f"record {index} prev does not match the previous record hash"
213	                )
214	        elif not isinstance(prev, str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(prev):
215	            # The first record's prev refers to the exporter's log and
216	            # cannot be checked against local state; require hash shape.
217	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} prev must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
218	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
219	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
220	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} seq must be an int")
221	        expected_seq += 1
222	        if seq != expected_seq:
223	            raise _invalid_batch(
224	                f"record {index} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
225	            )
226	        without_hash = {
227	            audit.DETAIL: record[audit.DETAIL],
228	            audit.KIND: record[audit.KIND],
229	            audit.PREV: prev,
230	            audit.SEQ: seq,
231	            audit.SOURCE: record[audit.SOURCE],
232	        }
233	        if digest != audit._record_hash(without_hash):
234	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} hash does not match its contents")
235	        expected_prev = digest
236	
237	    expected_next = expected_seq if records else data[AFTER]
238	    if data[NEXT] != expected_next:
239	        raise _invalid_batch("next must be the last record seq, or after when empty")
240	
241	    # The bytes must be the exact canonical compact encoding export_batch
242	    # produces: no whitespace, no non-canonical escapes, fixed key order.
243	    if _compact(data) + b"\n" != batch:
244	        raise _invalid_batch("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
245	    return data

248	def _restore_log(path: str, existed: bool, size: int) -> None:
249	    """Best-effort rollback of a failed append.
250	
251	    Append-mode writes only ever extend the file, so truncating back to
252	    the pre-call size restores the exact prior bytes; a file the failed
253	    call newly created is unlinked again.  Rollback errors are swallowed
254	    so the original :class:`OSError` propagates unchanged.
255	    """
256	    try:
257	        if existed:
258	            with open(path, "r+b") as handle:
259	                handle.truncate(size)
260	                handle.flush()
261	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
262	        else:
263	            os.unlink(path)
264	    except OSError:
265	        pass

268	def import_batch(path: str, batch: bytes) -> dict:
269	    """Validate a replication batch and append its suffix to the local log.
270	
271	    See the module docstring for the byte contract.  A ``path`` that is not
272	    a str or a ``batch`` that is not bytes raises :class:`TypeError`; any
273	    contract violation raises :class:`ValueError`.  The local log is read
274	    solely through :func:`audit.read`, and a corrupt log or filesystem
275	    error propagates as :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
276	    CorruptAuditError` or :class:`OSError`.  Any failure leaves the log
277	    byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was
278	    missing).
279	    """
280	    if not isinstance(path, str):
281	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
282	    if not isinstance(batch, bytes):
283	        raise TypeError("batch must be bytes")
284	
285	    data = _parse_batch(batch)
286	    after = data[AFTER]
287	    batch_records = data[RECORDS]
288	
289	    local_records = audit.read(path)
290	    last_seq = local_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if local_records else 0
291	
292	    if after > last_seq:
293	        return {NEED: [last_seq + 1, after], NEXT: last_seq, STATUS: STATUS_MISSING}
294	
295	    # Records with seq <= last_seq must already exist locally and match the
296	    # batch record field by field; everything past last_seq is appended.
297	    suffix: list[dict] = []
298	    for record in batch_records:
299	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
300	        if seq <= last_seq:
301	            local = local_records[seq - 1]
302	            if any(record[key] != local[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS):
303	                raise _invalid_batch(
304	                    f"record {seq} conflicts with the local record of the same seq"
305	                )
306	        else:
307	            if seq != last_seq + 1 + len(suffix):
308	                raise _invalid_batch("records past the local last seq must be contiguous")
309	            suffix.append(record)
310	
311	    if not suffix:
312	        return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_DUPLICATE}
313	
314	    # The first appended record must chain onto the local log's last hash
315	    # (or the zero hash for an empty log).
316	    local_last_hash = local_records[-1][audit.HASH] if local_records else audit._ZERO_HASH
317	    if suffix[0][audit.PREV] != local_last_hash:
318	        raise _invalid_batch(
319	            "first new record prev must match the local last record hash"
320	        )
321	
322	    lines = b"".join(
323	        audit._encode_line({key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS})
324	        for record in suffix
325	    )
326	    existed = os.path.exists(path)
327	    original_size = os.path.getsize(path) if existed else 0
328	    dir_fd: int | None = None
329	    try:
330	        with open(path, "ab") as handle:
331	            handle.write(lines)
332	            handle.flush()
333	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
334	        if not existed:
335	            dir_fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
336	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
337	    except OSError:
338	        _restore_log(path, existed, original_size)
339	        raise
340	    finally:
341	        if dir_fd is not None:
342	            os.close(dir_fd)
343	
344	    return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_APPLIED}
345

389	def _validated_apply_request(
390	    request: object,
391	) -> tuple[str, str, dict, dict]:
392	    """Validate an apply_remote request into (id, source, base, remote).
393	
394	    The states come back as fresh copies obeying the merge state contract,
395	    so type errors raised while validating them stay :class:`TypeError`.
396	    """
397	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
398	        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
399	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_KEYS):
400	        raise ValueError(
401	            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'source', 'base' "
402	            "and 'remote'"
403	        )
404	    request_id = request[ID]
405	    source = request[SOURCE]
406	    if not isinstance(request_id, str):
407	        raise TypeError("request id must be a str")
408	    if request_id == "":
409	        raise ValueError("request id must be non-empty")
410	    if not isinstance(source, str):
411	        raise TypeError("request source must be a str")
412	    if source == "":
413	        raise ValueError("request source must be non-empty")
414	    base_clock, base_records = merge._validated_state(request[BASE])
415	    remote_clock, remote_records = merge._validated_state(request[REMOTE])
416	    base = {merge.CLOCK: base_clock, merge.RECORDS: base_records}
417	    remote = {merge.CLOCK: remote_clock, merge.RECORDS: remote_records}
418	    return request_id, source, base, remote

421	def _request_digest(request_id: str, source: str, base: dict, remote: dict) -> str:
422	    """SHA-256 of the canonical compact encoding of the logical request."""
423	    ordered = {
424	        BASE: {merge.CLOCK: base[merge.CLOCK], merge.RECORDS: base[merge.RECORDS]},
425	        ID: request_id,
426	        REMOTE: {
427	            merge.CLOCK: remote[merge.CLOCK],
428	            merge.RECORDS: remote[merge.RECORDS],
429	        },
430	        SOURCE: source,
431	    }
432	    payload = json.dumps(
433	        ordered, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
434	    ).encode("utf-8")
435	    return _digest(payload)

438	def _serialize_ledger(
439	    state: dict, requests: dict[str, str], entries: list[dict]
440	) -> bytes:
441	    """Canonical ledger bytes: compact JSON, sorted keys, one trailing LF."""
442	    ledger = {
443	        AUDIT: [
444	            {key: entry[key] for key in _LEDGER_ENTRY_KEY_ORDER}
445	            for entry in entries
446	        ],
447	        REQUESTS: dict(requests),
448	        STATE_KEY: {
449	            merge.CLOCK: state[merge.CLOCK],
450	            merge.RECORDS: state[merge.RECORDS],
451	        },
452	        "version": LEDGER_VERSION,
453	    }
454	    text = json.dumps(
455	        ledger, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
456	    ) + "\n"
457	    return text.encode("utf-8")

460	def _is_digest(value: object) -> bool:
461	    return isinstance(value, str) and _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None

464	def _parse_ledger(raw: bytes) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, str], list[dict]]:
465	    """Validate every byte of a ledger into (state, requests, audit).
466	
467	    Any decoding, structural, state, index or chain violation raises
468	    :class:`ValueError`; in particular a type fault in the stored state is
469	    an on-disk corruption, not a :class:`TypeError`.
470	    """
471	    try:
472	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
473	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
474	        raise _ledger_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc
475	    try:
476	        data = json.loads(text)
477	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
478	        raise _ledger_invalid("is not valid JSON") from exc
479	
480	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
481	        raise _ledger_invalid("must be a JSON object")
482	    if set(data.keys()) != set(_LEDGER_TOP_KEYS):
483	        raise _ledger_invalid(
484	            "must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'requests', 'state' "
485	            "and 'version'"
486	        )
487	    version = data["version"]
488	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
489	        raise _ledger_invalid("version must be an int")
490	    if version != LEDGER_VERSION:
491	        raise _ledger_invalid("version must be the integer 1")
492	
493	    try:
494	        clock, records = merge._validated_state(data[STATE_KEY])
495	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
496	        raise _ledger_invalid(f"state is invalid: {exc}") from exc
497	    state = {merge.CLOCK: clock, merge.RECORDS: records}
498	
499	    raw_requests = data[REQUESTS]
500	    if not isinstance(raw_requests, dict):
501	        raise _ledger_invalid("requests must be a JSON object")
502	    requests: dict[str, str] = {}
503	    for bound_id, bound_digest in raw_requests.items():
504	        if not isinstance(bound_id, str) or bound_id == "":
505	            raise _ledger_invalid("requests keys must be non-empty str")
506	        if not _is_digest(bound_digest):
507	            raise _ledger_invalid(
508	                "requests values must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
509	            )
510	        requests[bound_id] = bound_digest
511	
512	    raw_entries = data[AUDIT]
513	    if not isinstance(raw_entries, list):
514	        raise _ledger_invalid("audit must be an array")
515	    entries: list[dict] = []
516	    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
517	    expected_seq = 1
518	    expected_before: str | None = None
519	    for position, entry in enumerate(raw_entries):
520	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
521	            raise _ledger_invalid(f"audit entry {position} must be an object")
522	        if set(entry.keys()) != _LEDGER_ENTRY_KEY_SET:
523	            raise _ledger_invalid(
524	                f"audit entry {position} must contain exactly the keys "
525	                "'after', 'before', 'id', 'seq' and 'source'"
526	            )
527	        after_digest = entry[AFTER]
528	        before_digest = entry[BEFORE]
529	        entry_id = entry[ID]
530	        seq = entry["seq"]
531	        entry_source = entry[SOURCE]
532	        if not _is_digest(after_digest):
533	            raise _ledger_invalid(
534	                f"audit entry {position} after must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
535	            )
536	        if not _is_digest(before_digest):
537	            raise _ledger_invalid(
538	                f"audit entry {position} before must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
539	            )
540	        if not isinstance(entry_id, str) or entry_id == "":
541	            raise _ledger_invalid(f"audit entry {position} id must be a non-empty str")
542	        if not isinstance(entry_source, str) or entry_source == "":
543	            raise _ledger_invalid(
544	                f"audit entry {position} source must be a non-empty str"
545	            )
546	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
547	            raise _ledger_invalid(f"audit entry {position} seq must be an int")
548	        if seq != expected_seq:
549	            raise _ledger_invalid(
550	                f"audit entry {position} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
551	            )
552	        if entry_id in seen_ids:
553	            raise _ledger_invalid(
554	                f"audit entry {position} repeats the already applied id {entry_id!r}"
555	            )
556	        if entry_id not in requests:
557	            raise _ledger_invalid(
558	                f"audit entry {position} id {entry_id!r} is missing from requests"
559	            )
560	        if expected_before is not None and before_digest != expected_before:
561	            raise _ledger_invalid(
562	                f"audit entry {position} before does not chain to the previous after"
563	            )
564	        entries.append(
565	            {
566	                AFTER: after_digest,
567	                BEFORE: before_digest,
568	                ID: entry_id,
569	                "seq": seq,
570	                SOURCE: entry_source,
571	            }
572	        )
573	        seen_ids.add(entry_id)
574	        expected_seq += 1
575	        expected_before = after_digest
576	
577	    if seen_ids != set(requests):
578	        raise _ledger_invalid("requests and audit must bind the same ids")
579	    if entries and entries[-1][AFTER] != _digest(_state_bytes(state)):
580	        raise _ledger_invalid("last audit after must hash the stored state")
581	
582	    # The bytes must be the single canonical compact encoding with sorted
583	    # keys and exactly one trailing newline.
584	    if not raw.endswith(b"\n") or raw.endswith(b"\n\n"):
585	        raise _ledger_invalid("must end with exactly one newline")
586	    if _serialize_ledger(state, requests, entries) != raw:
587	        raise _ledger_invalid("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
588	    return state, requests, entries

604	def _record_decision(
605	    local_clock: dict,
606	    local_record: list | None,
607	    remote_record: list,
608	) -> tuple[str, dict | None]:
609	    """Classify one remote record against the current local state."""
610	    need = merge._remote_need(remote_record, local_clock)
611	    if need:
612	        return STATUS_MISSING, need
613	    if local_record is None:
614	        return APPLY, None
615	    if local_record == remote_record:
616	        return STATUS_DUPLICATE, None
617	    if merge._dominates(remote_record[2], local_record[2]):
618	        return APPLY, None
619	    if merge._dominates(local_record[2], remote_record[2]):
620	        return STALE, None
621	    return CONFLICT, None

624	def _overall_status(decisions: list[str]) -> str:
625	    """Overall outcome with missing > conflict > stale > applied > duplicate.
626	
627	    Any ``missing``/``conflict``/``stale`` item dominates; otherwise the
628	    request applies as soon as at least one item applies (the rest being
629	    apply or duplicate), and a batch with nothing to do is duplicate.
630	    """
631	    for status in (STATUS_MISSING, CONFLICT, STALE):
632	        if status in decisions:
633	            return status
634	    return STATUS_APPLIED if APPLY in decisions else STATUS_DUPLICATE

637	def _rollback_ledger_write(
638	    path: str,
639	    tmp_path: str,
640	    backup_path: str,
641	    existed: bool,
642	    stage: str,
643	) -> None:
644	    """Best-effort rollback of a failed :func:`_atomic_write`.
645	
646	    ``stage`` records how far the transaction got: ``write`` (temporary
647	    file written), ``link`` (predecessor hard-linked aside), ``install``
648	    (temporary moved into place) or ``sync`` (the directory sync after
649	    install).  The predecessor is retained as a hard link rather than
650	    rewritten, so renaming it back restores the original file
651	    byte-for-byte (indeed as the same inode) even with no working fsync
652	    or free space left.  The directory is synced last so the recovery is
653	    durable.  Every recovery error is swallowed so the original
654	    exception propagates unchanged.
655	    """
656	    try:
657	        if stage == "sync":
658	            if existed:
659	                os.replace(backup_path, path)
660	            else:
661	                try:
662	                    os.unlink(path)
663	                except FileNotFoundError:
664	                    pass
665	        elif stage == "install":
666	            # The replacement did not run: the predecessor at path is
667	            # untouched; the backup link and temporary file are internal
668	            # artifacts to remove.
669	            try:
670	                os.unlink(backup_path)
671	            except FileNotFoundError:
672	                pass
673	            try:
674	                os.unlink(tmp_path)
675	            except FileNotFoundError:
676	                pass
677	        else:
678	            # write/link stages leave the predecessor in place.
679	            try:
680	                os.unlink(tmp_path)
681	            except FileNotFoundError:
682	                pass
683	            if stage == "link":
684	                try:
685	                    os.unlink(backup_path)
686	                except FileNotFoundError:
687	                    pass
688	        try:
689	            storage._fsync_dir(path)
690	        except OSError:
691	            pass
692	    except OSError:
693	        pass
694	
695	
696	def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
697	    """Durably replace ``path`` with ``payload`` as a single transaction.
698	
699	    The temporary file's write, flush and file sync, the replacement and
700	    the following directory sync all lie inside the boundary.  An existing
701	    predecessor is retained as a hard link at ``path + ".old"`` -- without
702	    ever removing ``path`` -- until the new file is installed and the
703	    directory has synced, so any :class:`OSError` rolls back by renaming
704	    that link back: the prior file returns byte-for-byte (as the same
705	    inode, with no rewriting and therefore no dependence on a working
706	    fsync or free space), and a path the call created is removed again.
707	    The rollback syncs the directory as well.  The original
708	    :class:`OSError` propagates unchanged, no ``.tmp``/``.old`` artifact is
709	    left behind and such artifacts (for example from a killed process) are
710	    never read as a ledger.  On success both the file and the directory
711	    have been synced.
712	    """
713	    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"
714	    backup_path = path + ".old"
715	    existed = os.path.exists(path)
716	    # Retained artifacts from earlier interrupted calls are internal and
717	    # must never stand in the way of a fresh transaction (the temporary
718	    # name is overwritten by the open below).
719	    try:
720	        os.unlink(backup_path)
721	    except FileNotFoundError:
722	        pass
723	
724	    stage = "write"
725	    try:
726	        with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
727	            handle.write(payload)
728	            handle.flush()
729	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
730	        if existed:
731	            stage = "link"
732	            os.link(path, backup_path)
733	        stage = "install"
734	        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
735	        stage = "sync"
736	        storage._fsync_dir(path)
737	    except BaseException:
738	        _rollback_ledger_write(path, tmp_path, backup_path, existed, stage)
739	        raise
740	
741	    # The new ledger is durable from this point on; the retained
742	    # predecessor link is internal cleanup only.  Its removal (and the
743	    # matching directory sync) is best-effort and never undoes a commit.
744	    if existed:
745	        try:
746	            os.unlink(backup_path)
747	            storage._fsync_dir(path)
748	        except OSError:
749	            pass

752	def apply_remote(path: str, request: dict) -> dict:
753	    """Persistently apply one remote state request to the ledger at ``path``.
754	
755	    ``request`` must contain exactly the keys ``id`` and ``source`` (both
756	    non-empty str) and ``base`` and ``remote`` (states obeying the
757	    :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` contract).  ``path`` is a version-1
758	    ledger; when it is missing the current state is taken to be ``base``
759	    with empty request/audit indexes, otherwise the stored ``state``,
760	    ``requests`` and ``audit`` are fully validated before anything else.
761	
762	    An unknown ``id`` whose current state differs from ``base`` returns
763	    ``stale`` without touching the filesystem.  A known ``id`` whose bound
764	    request digest matches replays as ``duplicate``: the verdict comes from
765	    the saved binding alone, so the result is the same immediately or after
766	    later successful commits.  Its items list every remote record in
767	    ascending key order, each already ``duplicate`` with ``need`` an empty
768	    mapping, ``receipt`` is ``None`` and the ledger bytes are unchanged.  A
769	    known ``id`` presented with different contents raises
770	    :class:`ValueError`.

775	    ``missing`` and its item's ``need`` lists the closed intervals still

779	
780	    The overall status follows the precedence ``missing``, ``conflict``,

801	    """
802	    if not isinstance(path, str):

818	        items = [
